title: Ko'pik
subtitle: Proves a gas-equipment leak test was really done, from a video of soapy joints.
story: After fitting methane or propane equipment, the technician brushes soapy water on every joint and films it. Ko'pik checks every joint was covered, spots bubbles that grow (a leak) and saves a dated record tied to the gas cylinder.
why: Gas leaks in cars can cause fires and explosions. The rules track cylinders but say nothing about proving the leak test, and a third of used-car listings run on gas.

An inspection centre reviews tests remotely
An insurer checks a car's gas safety record
buyers: Gas-conversion workshops and inspection centres.

title: BallonID
subtitle: Reads a gas cylinder's stamped label and says if it is too old or untested.
story: Every gas cylinder has numbers stamped into the metal: serial, dates, pressure and gas type. They are hard to read under rust and paint. BallonID takes two photos lit from the side, reads the stamp and applies the official rules: refill, retest or refuse.
why: An out-of-date or wrong cylinder can explode; in Fergana a propane cylinder filled with methane did. Today checks look up the car's plate, not the cylinder itself.
uses: A filling station checks the cylinder before refuelling
An inspector reads stamps in seconds
A car buyer checks a gas-converted car
buyers: Inspection centres, car inspectors and gas stations.

why: After a crash and repair, panels rarely line up perfectly, so uneven gaps reveal hidden accidents. Inspectors check this by eye today.

A trade-in desk prices repaired cars correctly

title: ChargeMD
subtitle: Explains a charger's error message in plain language, from a photo.
story: Public chargers often show error codes in Chinese or English that drivers cannot understand. The driver photographs the screen; ChargeMD explains the problem, says what to do, and reports it to the operator.
why: An EV taxi stuck at a broken charger loses income. Operators also learn which chargers fail, helping build a reliable uptime map.
uses: A taxi driver fixes a simple charging error on the spot
An operator gets precise fault reports
Drivers see which chargers really work
buyers: EV taxi fleets and charging operators.

title: YardAudit
subtitle: Counts and checks a dealer's cars against the bank's list, from a walk-around video.
story: Banks lend money to dealers against the cars in their yard. The bank's agent walks the yard filming; YardAudit reads every plate and VIN and compares them with the pledged list to find missing cars.
why: If a dealer sells pledged cars without telling the bank, the loan loses its security. Counting by hand is slow and error-prone.
uses: A bank audits a dealer's stock in 10 minutes
An import yard tracks cars without plates
A lender spots missing cars early
buyers: Banks and leasing firms that lend to dealers, and import yards.
